headline: 12 killed, 309 injured in Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
summary: Two Bangladeshis are among the dead in the deadly strike on King Khalid International Airport, sparking international condemnation.
details: A deadly attack by Houthi rebels on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has left at least 12 people dead and 309 others injured.
The victims include four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, and one citizen each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed deep concern and shock, stating that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law.
The Bangladesh government has strongly condemned the attack and the casualties, while efforts are underway to identify the deceased nationals.
The strike is the third Houthi attack on the Riyadh airport this week, causing significant disruption to air travel.
Several flights from Dhaka to Riyadh were cancelled following the airport's temporary closure and the blast.
In Riyadh, schools have shifted to online classes for one week following the security incident.
caption:
12 dead and over 300 injured after Houthi rebels strike a major Saudi airport. Two Bangladeshis are among the victims.

A deadly attack by Houthi rebels on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has left at least 12 people dead and 309 others injured.

The victims include four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, and one citizen each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, and Egypt.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed deep concern and shock, stating that attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are a violation of international law.

The Bangladesh government has strongly condemned the attack and the casualties, while efforts are underway to identify the deceased nationals.

The strike is the third Houthi attack on the Riyadh airport this week, causing significant disruption to air travel.

Several flights from Dhaka to Riyadh were cancelled following the airport's temporary closure and the blast.

In Riyadh, schools have shifted to online classes for one week following the security incident.

Source: Jamuna TV, Dhaka Tribune, bdnews24.com, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline: India court orders release of 'cockroach' movement leaders
summary: Abhijeet Dipke and two other CJP leaders were released by an executive magistrate's court on the condition they maintain peace for one year.
details: The founder of India's youth-led 'cockroach' movement and two other leaders were released on Sunday after being detained to prevent a major protest against the election commissioner.
caption:
Released on condition: Three leaders of India's 'cockroach' movement are free after being detained to thwart a major protest.

The founder of India's youth-led 'cockroach' movement and two other leaders were released on Sunday after being detained to prevent a major protest against the election commissioner.
